To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the baryon density, n, at mu_B = 300 MeV and T = 100 MeV is (2.1 +- 0.4) fm^-3 and the pressure, P, is (0.2 +- 0.2) GeV^4.
the equation of state is insensitive to quark masses, and the bulk isothermal susceptibility is consistent with the Stefan-Boltzmann limit.
the equation of state at finite chemical potential is insensitive to the light-quark mass, and that the critical point of the QCD phase diagram lies at mu_B= 350 +/- 50 MeV and T= 160 +/- 20 MeV.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the equation of state (EOS) of two-flavour QCD at finite temperature and chemical potential.
the thermodynamics and phase diagram of QCD at non-zero baryon chemical potential and temperature.
the study of QCD at high temperature, and finite chemical potential, in the vicinity of the critical end-point.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
QCD is a critical theory with a critical point at (mu_B/T)_c = 0.45 +/- 0.05 and kappa = 1.2 +/- 0.2.

lattice QCD is consistent with the hypothesis of a second order phase transition at a critical temperature T_c=170(5) MeV, with critical exponent beta=0.35(3) and with critical chemical potential mu_c=350(25) MeV.

the QCD equation of state at finite mu_B and finite T is well described by the Stefan-Boltzmann law for the pressure, with the baryon density given by the Stefan-Boldtzman law with a correction term which is independent of the quark mass and of the order of 10% for the range of T and chemical potential studied.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the equation of state for QCD at finite mu_B and T, is well described by a first order phase transition with a small latent heat and a large bulk modulus.
QCD at finite mu_B and T is in the same universality class as the three-dimensional Ising model, but with an effective coupling which is larger at finite chemical potential.
the equation of state is well behaved and that the bulk isothermal sound speed squared is close to 0.5.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we find that n and delta P have the same critical behaviour as in QCD at zero chemical potential.
the baryon chemical potential is a natural scale of QCD at low T, and that QCD at low temperatures is a critical theory.
the critical chemical potential is mu_B = 0 and that kappa is negative over a range of temperatures, which implies that QCD is in the critical phase of the QCD phase diagram at finite T and mu_B.
